## Immutable source authority
- Intake commit: `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`
- Snapshot documentation commit: `40af815bf0`
- Original source bytes: [`doc/2026-11-13T01-34-11Z_design_fleet_ca_credentials_secrets/source-snapshots/intake-34faffbff2/sources`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/tree/40af815bf0/doc/2026-11-13T01-34-11Z_design_fleet_ca_credentials_secrets/source-snapshots/intake-34faffbff2/sources)

## Authored proposal metadata (administrative; not dropped)
```json
{"kind_normalization":{"publisher_kind":"implementation","reason":"Owns additive Fleet library identity/reference types and a minimal adapter with focused API tests; the deliverable is code, not another design stage."},"original_depends_on":["TRACE-02"],"original_id":"ARCH-01","original_kind":"design+implementation+test","original_parent":"#9157","source_provenance":{"auxiliary_source":"doc/2026-11-13T01-34-11Z_design_fleet_ca_credentials_secrets/source-snapshots/intake-34faffbff2/note.md","repository":"developing-today/code","snapshot_commit":"40af815bf0","source_commit":"34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e","source_integrity":"doc/2026-11-13T01-34-11Z_design_fleet_ca_credentials_secrets/source-integrity.md","source_root":"doc/2026-11-13T01-34-11Z_design_fleet_ca_credentials_secrets/source-snapshots/intake-34faffbff2/sources"},"urgency_band":"High"}
```

## Why / user outcome
Establish one stable runtime library seam for secret reads and identity/reference resolution. Preserve existing CLI behavior while making canonical identity independent of mutable names, paths, or provider-native IDs. Reading a secret must not grant write, replication, export, escrow, or signing authority.

## Current repository evidence
At source commit `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs` implements a name-only resolver with redacted `SecretValue`, source order, and broker/BWS fallback; `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs` implements only `get` and `list`. There is no typed canonical identity or scope/API. `fleet secrets get` intentionally prints the requested value to stdout; this is a caller-facing contract, not diagnostic logging. `cargo test --locked -p fleet-secrets` passed 16 tests on 2026-11-12, invoked bare with no resource wrapper or durable log.

## Scope and affected surface
Define additive public types and focused API tests in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/**`, with only the minimum `fleet` adapter needed. TRACE-02 owns the V1 CLI/profile golden corpus; this proposal consumes that legacy oracle and does not duplicate fixture/test ownership. Do not implement provider adapters, credential serialization/reconciliation, cache daemon changes, writer/admin APIs, PKI, generation, production reads, or a new crate. Coordinate the canonical credential schema with SEC-02; this seam defines identity/reference behavior, not its full record schema. A typed `RootPrivate` rejection does not protect V1 broker refresh or name-only BWS fallback: ROOT-09/OPS-10 must prove the legacy paths cannot access escrow scope before any copy. Trusted scope/native-ID exclusion or a separately least-privileged provider grant is required; a caller-supplied class or mutable sidecar is not sufficient. Affected files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs`, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs`, and focused tests under those crates; no provider config or data migration.

## API and behavior contract
Proposed typed shape:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
pub struct CredentialId(pub uuid::Uuid); // opaque canonical identity
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
pub struct SecretAlias { pub scope: ScopeId, pub name: String } // mutable locator
pub async fn resolve_alias(alias: &SecretAlias, cancel: CancellationToken)
    -> Result<CredentialId, AliasError>;
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
pub struct SecretRef { pub id: CredentialId, pub field: Option<FieldId> }
pub struct ResolutionContext {
    pub purpose: Purpose,
    pub offline_intent: OfflineIntent,
    pub required_assurance: AssuranceRequirement,
    pub caller_max_age: Option<Duration>, // only tightens stored policy
}
/// Private fields, loaded by the trusted server policy source, not supplied per request.
pub struct RevocationPolicy { /* opaque, server-owned policy */ }
pub struct AuthoritativeCredentialPolicy { /* private fields: stored class, revocation policy,
    verified provider/account/project/vault/native-ID binding, max age, offline permission,
    assurance floor */ }
#[async_trait]
pub trait AuthoritativePolicySource: Send + Sync {
    async fn load(&self, id: CredentialId, cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<AuthoritativeCredentialPolicy, PolicyError>;
}
pub enum RevocationState { CurrentNotRevoked, Revoked, Unknown }
pub enum FreshnessDecision { Fresh, Degraded { reason: DegradedReason } }
pub enum DegradedReason { PolicyAuthorizedOfflineReplica, BoundedStaleUse }
pub struct ResolvedSecret {
    pub value: SecretBytes, // redacted Debug; no Clone/Serialize/Display
    pub source: ProviderId,
    pub native_revision: Option<Revision>,
    pub fetched_at: SystemTime,
    pub source_age: Duration,
    pub revocation: RevocationState,
    pub freshness: FreshnessDecision,
}
#[async_trait]
pub trait SecretStore: Send + Sync {
    async fn get(&self, id: CredentialId, field: Option<&FieldId>,
                 cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<ProviderValue, ProviderError>;
}
pub struct Resolver { /* trusted policy source + injected stores/cache; no writer/signer */ }
impl Resolver {
    pub async fn resolve(&self, r: &SecretRef, context: &ResolutionContext,
                         cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<ResolvedSecret, ResolveError>;
}
```
The per-call context contains purpose/offline intent/required assurance and optional max-age tightening, never stored class or revocation authority. Stored class/policy and scope/native binding come from the resolver's trusted policy source. Caller constraints can only tighten; self-labels or mutable sidecars cannot lower class. RootPrivate and RootSigning are denied by the ordinary resolver. Result includes source age and explicit fresh/degraded decision; any degraded success includes a typed reason. Revoked, policy-denied or insufficient-assurance values fail closed. PERF-02 owns freshness/revocation semantics; this packet defines the shared shape, not a second resolver or semantic owner.
## Measurable acceptance
1. A deterministic in-memory fake resolves by `CredentialId` without process spawn, filesystem or network.
2. Alias rename and provider/path relocation preserve `CredentialId`; same display name under different scopes never aliases.
3. Context exposes purpose/offline intent/required assurance and optional caller max age; trusted policy returns authoritative class/revocation/scope-binding and the caller cannot weaken it.
4. A fake-clock matrix varies stored class, purpose, online/offline request, assurance, revocation state and age for one logical ID. Oracle outcomes are fresh allow, bounded policy-authorized degraded use with explicit reason/source age, or denial. Revoked/high-risk deny overrides cache; no stale auto-fallback.
5. Ordinary typed resolver denies RootPrivate and its cache/prefetch/equality-index path. Legacy broker/BWS root exclusion is a separate ROOT-09/OPS-10 rollout gate and must be proved before any escrow copy.
6. API remains compatible with legacy CLI; TRACE-02 owns V1 golden stdout/stderr/exit fixtures and fixture/test work.
## Negative tests and oracle
Negative: alias collision, scope mismatch, path/name-derived ID, empty value, malformed provider response, caller attempt to downgrade authoritative class/assurance/revocation or self-assert RootPrivate/offline permission, revoked or unknown status under a must-check policy, and stale automatic fallback all fail closed. Oracle: fake provider plus authoritative policy registry and fake clock, reference policy-combination model, compile-time trait assertions (no `Serialize`/`Clone` on secret values), and output sentinel scan. CLI byte/exit oracles belong only to TRACE-02.

## Security and environment
Synthetic values only. No live provider access. Diagnostic output never contains value/token. Explicit stdout result remains permitted only as the legacy caller contract; callers needing stronger output control require a separate output policy.

## Dependencies, size, priority, lifecycle
Parent #9157; depends on #9156 TRACE-02 for the V1 compatibility oracle; SEC-02 consumes the opaque ID seam. Complexity M; V2; proposed High / urgency 450; Backlog.

## Rollback and recovery
Additive types can be removed while retaining legacy resolver and `get/list`. No persistent schema or external state changes. If typed API parity fails, keep old chain as default and disable the new API path; use TRACE-02’s V1 corpus as the CLI rollback oracle.

## Open decisions
Pick UUID representation/alias registry location only with SEC-02; do not store canonical identity in provider name/path or add a dependency/crate solely for an alias map.

## Priority semantics
The numeric `urgency` field is the shared charter intrinsic scale (lower is sooner); this score is High, distinct from importance, blocker, stage and dispatch. It is not the Project/queue priority. Do not change PM schema; any publisher maps High to queue priority 20 while retaining this numeric score and band in metadata/body.

- Snapshot documentation commit: `40af815bf0`
- Original source bytes: [`doc/2026-11-13T01-34-11Z_design_fleet_ca_credentials_secrets/source-snapshots/intake-34faffbff2/sources`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/tree/40af815bf0/doc/2026-11-13T01-34-11Z_design_fleet_ca_credentials_secrets/source-snapshots/intake-34faffbff2/sources)

## Authored proposal metadata (administrative; not dropped)
```json
{"kind_normalization":{"publisher_kind":"implementation","reason":"Owns typed signer-session and artifact-sink interface implementation/tests in the reusable crypto seam when dependency closure allows; this is a code interface deliverable, not a standalone design-only issue."},"original_depends_on":["OPS-01"],"original_id":"ARCH-06","original_kind":"design+interface-test","original_parent":"#9157","source_provenance":{"auxiliary_source":"doc/2026-11-13T01-34-11Z_design_fleet_ca_credentials_secrets/source-snapshots/intake-34faffbff2/note.md","repository":"developing-today/code","snapshot_commit":"40af815bf0","source_commit":"34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e","source_integrity":"doc/2026-11-13T01-34-11Z_design_fleet_ca_credentials_secrets/source-integrity.md","source_root":"doc/2026-11-13T01-34-11Z_design_fleet_ca_credentials_secrets/source-snapshots/intake-34faffbff2/sources"},"urgency_band":"High"}
```

## Why / user outcome
Define only the shared authority interfaces for signer use and artifact output. An ordinary secret reference, inventory result, escrow read, or possession of key bytes must never confer signing authority. PKI graph construction and all algorithm/client implementation remain owned by #9163/#9164/#9162; general file transactions remain #9165.

## Current repository evidence
At `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, Fleet has no signer, artifact-authority, or PKI module. `pkgs/id` Iroh endpoint identity is a separate identity type, not a root CA authorization contract. Parent ADR-S01 and the architecture challenge A-2 require transaction binding and anti-replay. ROOT-05 and CERT-03 already own PKI-specific implementation of that contract; this proposal owns only shared interface shape.

## Scope and technical boundaries
Specify typed signer authorization, session consumption, signer result/receipt and artifact sink authorization. Do not implement CA/issuer/leaf graph, algorithm registry/backends, PKI profiles, provider escrow, publication, output file transaction, or new CLI. The cohesive shared crypto contract may live in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-crypto/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs,tests/authorization.rs}` only if measured dependency closure makes it reusable by both generation and PKI; wire it opt-in in `pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml` and `pkgs/fleet/default.nix`. Do not create separate crates for authorization, signer, or artifact nouns. Affected files, if dependency closure justifies code: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-crypto/Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `tests/authorization.rs`, and optional wiring in `pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml`/`pkgs/fleet/default.nix`; otherwise this is a documentation-only contract in this design packet.

## Proposed interface
The exact signing payload is prepared before authorization. Authority-bearing values have private constructors and no implicit `Clone`.
```rust
pub struct SigningAuthorization { // private fields; minted only by authority service
    root_key: AuthorizedKeyIdentity, // fingerprint/handle
    subject_spki: PublicKeyIdentity,
    signature_algorithm: SignatureAlgorithm,
    serial: Option<SerialNumber>,
    signed_payload_digest: Digest, // exact final TBS/message bytes
    profile: ProfileId,
    purpose: KeyPurpose,
    validity: ExactValidity,
    artifact_plan_digest: Digest,
    destinations: Vec<AuthorizedDestination>,
    expires_at: SystemTime,
    transaction_id: TransactionId,
    nonce: SingleUseNonce,
}
pub struct PreparedSigningTuple { /* private: SPKI, serial, exact TBS and plan digests */ }
pub struct PreparedIssuance { /* immutable final TBS + artifacts; private fields */ }
pub struct SignerSession { /* private, one validated authorization tuple */ }
pub struct DurableTupleClaim { /* private, atomic single-winner, non-Clone */ }
pub struct OutputAuthorization { /* private, exact plan/class/destination/expiry, non-Clone */ }
#[async_trait]
pub trait SigningAuthorizationPort: Send + Sync {
    async fn authorize_prepared(&self, tuple: &PreparedSigningTuple,
                                cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<SignerSession, AuthorizationError>;
}
#[async_trait]
pub trait DurableAuthorizationLedger: Send + Sync {
    async fn consume_once(&self, session: &mut SignerSession, tuple_digest: Digest,
                          cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<DurableTupleClaim, ClaimError>;
    async fn record_result(&self, claim: DurableTupleClaim,
                           result: SigningReceiptOrUncertain) -> Result<(), LedgerError>;
}
#[async_trait]
pub trait Signer: Send + Sync {
    async fn sign(&self, claim: &DurableTupleClaim, exact_tbs: &[u8],
                  cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<SignatureReceipt, SignError>;
}
#[async_trait]
pub trait OutputAuthorizationPort: Send + Sync {
    async fn authorize_output(&self, plan: &ArtifactPlan, artifact: &ClassifiedArtifact,
                              cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<OutputAuthorization, OutputAuthorizationError>;
}
#[async_trait]
pub trait ArtifactSink: Send {
    async fn write(&mut self, authorization: &OutputAuthorization,
                   artifact: ClassifiedArtifact, cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<ArtifactReceipt, SinkError>;
}
pub struct PkiEngine { /* PKI profiles/graph; no embedded signer authority */ }
impl PkiEngine {
    pub async fn prepare_leaf(&self, req: LeafRequest, serials: &dyn SerialLedger,
                              clock: &dyn Clock, cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<PreparedIssuance, PkiError>;
    pub async fn sign_prepared(&self, prepared: PreparedIssuance,
                               session: &mut SignerSession, claim: DurableTupleClaim,
                               signer: &dyn Signer, cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<SignedIssuance, PkiError>;
    pub async fn issue_leaf(&self, req: LeafRequest,
                            authorization: &dyn SigningAuthorizationPort,
                            serials: &dyn SerialLedger, ledger: &dyn DurableAuthorizationLedger,
                            signer: &dyn Signer, clock: &dyn Clock, cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<IssuedCertificate, PkiError>;
    pub async fn issue_root(&self, req: RootRequest, root_key: ExplicitRootKeyRef,
                            ceremony: &RootKeyCreationAuthorization,
                            authorization: &dyn SigningAuthorizationPort,
                            signer: &dyn Signer, ledger: &dyn DurableAuthorizationLedger,
                            cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<RootArtifact, PkiError>;
}
```
The `issue_leaf` convenience helper prepares/reserves first and requests authorization only after SPKI, serial, exact TBS and artifact-plan digest are known; it never accepts a prefilled grant for unknown bytes. A dry run may show estimates/placeholders but cannot reserve a serial or mint final-TBS authorization. Root signing always names an explicit root key and separate key-creation/storage ceremony approval. A grant is single-tuple by default; multi-use must enumerate every final tuple. The ledger atomically consumes once before invoking the signer. Output authorization is separately minted for the exact plan/class/destination and cannot be derived from a signer grant.
## Measurable acceptance
1. An exact tuple grant binds root fingerprint/handle, subject SPKI, algorithm, serial, exact TBS digest, profile/purpose, validity, plan digest, destinations, expiry and transaction ID; mismatch is rejected before signing.
2. Two concurrent consumers race for one tuple; exactly one durable claim succeeds and signer invocation count is at most one.
3. Crash injection before claim, after claim/before signer call, after call/before receipt, and after receipt proves no duplicate invocation. A lost result with no authoritative status remains uncertain and blocked.
4. The high-level leaf helper only asks the authorization port after preparing final SPKI/serial/TBS/plan. Root helper requires an explicit key reference and separate ceremony approval; neither accepts a generic default signer.
5. Compile-fail/API tests show no signing without validated session/claim and no classified/private artifact write without `OutputAuthorization`; wrong destination, plan, class, expiry, or replay yields zero signer/sink calls.
6. ROOT-03/ROOT-04 synthetic signing uses this seam; their proposal dependencies include ARCH-06 and ROOT-05, or their bodies specify the same enforcement and tests. Direct signer bypass fails review/tests.
7. The interface stays in-memory and async; no private key bytes enter authority objects or receipts.
## Negative tests and oracle
Reject ambient/default signer discovery, signer substitution/fingerprint mismatch, changed plan digest, subject SPKI or algorithm mismatch, wrong purpose/profile, altered validity, unauthorized output/escrow destination, expired grant, replay, signer handle passed as `SecretRef`, or public-only grant used for private output. Oracle: model-based durable tuple state machine, synchronized two-consumer race, crash/fault injection, exact authorization/TBS digest comparison, fake invocation counters, authoritative-status fake, compile-fail/API fixtures showing no sign without claim and no private write without output grant, and redacted receipt golden fixture.

## Security and environment
Synthetic authorization and fake keys only. No production signing, key export, custody, DNS, trust-store or provider action.

## Dependencies, size, priority, lifecycle
Parent #9157; consumes plan/receipt schema OPS-01. Complexity M; V2 shared contract; proposed High / urgency 500; Backlog. ROOT-05 and CERT-03 implement PKI-specific adapters; GEN-04 consumes only after independent review.

## Rollback and recovery
Interface is additive and authority-denying by default. Disable fake adapter/feature if the model fails; do not relax mismatch checks to retain compatibility. No persistent state or production key changes.

## Open decisions
Concrete authorization token format, external approval ceremony and HSM attestation remain domain implementation decisions. The binding fields, durable atomic consume point, uncertain-status behavior, and refusal conditions are fixed; do not duplicate or weaken them in ROOT-05/CERT-03. ROOT-03/ROOT-04 synthetic graph fixtures must use this same authorized seam rather than direct signing.

## Priority semantics
The numeric `urgency` field is the shared charter intrinsic scale (lower is sooner); this score is High, distinct from importance, blocker, stage and dispatch. It is not the Project/queue priority. Do not change PM schema; any publisher maps High to queue priority 20 while retaining this numeric score and band in metadata/body.

Keep Fleet as the sole multicall CLI and make compiled, invocation-profile, and effective capabilities accurate as secrets/generation/PKI domains arrive. No competing CLI, CA server, or duplicate command registry.

## Current repository evidence
At `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, `fleet-registry` is std-only and separates compiled/profile/effective capability sets. Existing domains have `secrets` but no `cert`/`pki` or `generate`. `fleet` Cargo features build full/serve/connect; `fleet-connect` is proxy-only with a stripped artifact hard cap of 2 MiB and target 1.5 MiB (`pkgs/fleet/default.nix`). ## Acceptance criteria
1. A committed matrix enumerates compiled, invocation-profile and effective capability for full, serve, connect, consumer-min, agent and admin profiles.
2. Missing capability uses the existing registry unavailable behavior; help remains discoverable and accurately states prerequisites.
3. `fleet secrets get/list` stdout, stderr, exit semantics and broker/BWS order remain compatible. Secret stdout remains intentional and only diagnostics are redacted.
4. Command descriptors resolve from one registry source; help, JSON capability output, completion and dispatch agree.
5. No new profile name widens compiled capabilities; configuration cannot enable an uncompiled domain.
6. Existing `fleet-connect` has no secrets/crypto/PKI/generator dependency and remains ≤2 MiB stripped, with 1.5 MiB target.

## Negative tests and oracle
Negative: invocation alias requests capability absent from binary, connect invokes secrets/cert/generate, config enables uncompiled feature, command advertised available without implementation, and command aliases produce distinct semantics. Oracle: capability golden matrix, current CLI output fixtures, smoke invocations and Nix final-artifact size gate.

## Security and environment
Build/test only. No deployment, signing, provider access, secret mutation, trust/DNS change or new schedule. New commands remain unavailable stubs until their owner deliverables land.

Parent #9157; depends on ARCH-01/06 shared APIs and domain descriptors GEN-01/CERT-01 with soft coordination (not a blockedBy edge) with generated-help owner OPS-05. Complexity M; V2; proposed High / urgency 450; Backlog.

Revert only additive descriptors/feature edges; preserve current domain entries and variants. Verify `fleet-connect` and `get/list` fixtures after rollback. Do not remove a domain implementation owned by another proposal.

## Open decisions
Exact Nix artifact/profile packaging waits for measured dependency closure in ARCH-10. Capability naming/help additions wait for GEN-01/CERT-01/SEC domain schemas; avoid duplicate aliases.

## Priority semantics
The numeric `urgency` field is the shared charter intrinsic scale (lower is sooner); this score is High, distinct from importance, blocker, stage and dispatch. It is not the Project/queue priority. ```

## Why / user outcome
Provide one typed library resolver for heterogeneous input references and one typed output-target plan consumed by existing Fleet commands. Users and embedded callers can select inputs/outputs without each domain inventing string guessing, format routing or private-output behavior. This is not a new CLI or a second secret resolver.

## Current repository evidence
At pinned census commit `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, Fleet has a broker/BWS name resolver but no shared `InputRef`/`OutputTarget` module. ARCH-01 owns SecretRef/policy; ARCH-06 owns signer/output authorization; OPS-04 owns safe file/archive writes. Those are consumed, not reimplemented here.

## Scope and owned files/interfaces
Implement one cohesive reusable `fleet-io` crate because CLI, PKI, generation and embedded Rust have multiple real consumers of the same resolution/selection seam; do not create a crate per source or format. Proposed files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-io/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs,tests/input_ref.rs,tests/output_target.rs}`, plus opt-in workspace/consumer feature wiring. It owns typed normalization and target planning only. It delegates secret reads to ARCH-01, authorization to ARCH-06, and physical file/archive transactions to OPS-04.

## API/CLI behavior
```rust
pub enum InputRef {
    File(PathBuf), DirectoryManifest(PathBuf), Archive(PathBuf), Stdin,
    Structured { format: InputFormat, bytes: Vec<u8> },
    PkiFingerprint(PublicFingerprint), LogicalId(CredentialId),
    SecretUri(QualifiedSecretUri), DefaultInventory(NonRootInventoryRef),
    ExplicitSignerHandle(ExplicitKeyRef), InMemory(MemoryArtifactRef),
}
pub enum OutputTarget {
    File(PathBuf), Directory(PathBuf), Archive(PathBuf),
    Stdout(PublicOutputMode), ProviderStore(ProviderId, ScopeId),
    Memory(SinkHandle), None,
}
pub async fn resolve_input(&self, request: InputRequest, cancel: CancellationToken)
    -> Result<ResolvedInput, InputError>;
pub async fn plan_output(&self, target: OutputTarget, artifact: ClassifiedArtifact,
                         cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<OutputPlan, OutputError>;
```
`InputResolver` delegates SecretUri/LogicalId to ARCH-01; a signer-handle reference is a locator only and cannot create signing authority. DefaultInventory is permitted only for explicit non-root read purposes. OutputTarget is a plan, not a writer: confidential outputs require ARCH-06 `OutputAuthorization`; ProviderStore writes also require provider capability/operation grant, and file/archive commit goes through OPS-04. Example at an existing Fleet domain surface: `fleet cert bundle inspect --input <typed-ref> --dry-run --json`; no standalone executable or new command family is added by this packet.

Typed errors: `InvalidReference`, `AmbiguousInput { candidates: RedactedCandidate[] }`, `UnsupportedFormat`, `NotFound`, `ScopeDenied`, `PolicyDenied`, `UnsafeArchive`, `CapabilityUnavailable`, `Cancelled`, `Unavailable`. Ambiguous errors expose only redacted candidate refs, never values.

## Measurable acceptance
1. Normalize file, directory/manifest, archive, stdin, structured bytes, PKI fingerprint, stable ID, qualified secret URI, non-root inventory, explicit signer handle and in-memory artifact into typed variants.
2. Ambiguous matching sources fail with typed candidate diagnostics; no first-match, provider-speed or path/name guessing.
3. Secret resolution delegates to ARCH-01. Root default-inventory lookup and signer authority are denied; explicit signer handles do not act as grants.
4. OutputTarget covers file/directory/archive/stdout/provider-store/memory/none and public/private classification. Private bytes require exact plan/class/destination `OutputAuthorization`; public/stdout defaults exclude private material.
5. Archive parsing is bounded by total bytes, entry count and expansion; traversal, outside symlinks, duplicate normalized paths and bombs reject before extraction.
6. All candidate selection is explicit/deterministic; same label across input kinds is ambiguous unless a typed selector uniquely resolves it.
7. No filesystem/network/subprocess is required for an in-memory reference/plan; no dependency cycle with fleet-secrets, PKI or CLI.

## Negative tests and oracle
Property tests round-trip typed refs/aliases and ensure scopes never collide; a reference selector model determines exact unique/ambiguous outcomes. Fuzz archive parsing. Negative fixtures cover path/archive same basename, duplicate URI/ID candidate, root lookup through DefaultInventory, caller-supplied public classification, signer-handle-as-authority, private stdout without grant, unauthorized ProviderStore, path traversal, symlink escape, duplicate archive entries, excessive expansion and cancellation. Oracle: reference selector output, fixture hashes/entry set and zero provider/sink calls on denial.

## Security and safe environment
Synthetic inputs/targets only. No live providers, keys, stores, archive exports, file mutations, DNS/trust operations or credentials. RootPrivate stays out of ordinary resolution and caching. This is a V2 proposal; no V1 implementation is implied.

## Dependencies, priority, lifecycle, size, stage
Parent #9157; hard dependencies ARCH-01, ARCH-06 and OPS-04. Estimated size/complexity L; V2 foundation; Backlog; intrinsic urgency 600 (High), separate from importance/stage/queue projection.

## Failure, rollback, recovery
Resolution/planning is side-effect free until a separately authorized adapter operation. Invalid/ambiguous/unsafe input fails before read/write. Disable the optional fleet-io consumer edge to roll back; preserve V1 resolver and all existing commands.

## Open decisions
Pin archive parser/limits after dependency/license/security review. Keep `fleet-io` one cohesive seam only if multiple consumers and dependency closure remain demonstrated; otherwise keep the module in the narrowest shared library. No per-format crate split.
stage: V2 foundation; integrated by existing Fleet domain commands
title: Implement the unified input-reference and output-target resolver with typed selectors

## Why / user outcome
Provide one embedded Rust composition facade so humans, scripts and Rust callers use the same typed operation semantics without invoking the Fleet binary internally. It composes domain-owned operations and injected ports; it does not become a domain-logic god object or a second authorization authority.

## Current repository evidence
At pinned census commit `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, Fleet has a multicall binary and separate crates such as `fleet-secrets`, registry, config and queue, but no reusable `FleetContext` composition library. `fleet-secrets` is a name resolver, not a complete application context. ARCH-01/06/07/12 define runtime read, signer/artifact authority, CLI registry and input/output planning seams; domain proposals own PKI, generation, credential schema, reconciliation, sinks and receipts.

## Scope and owned files/interfaces
Add one reusable `fleet-context` facade crate because CLI and embedded Rust callers need the same cross-domain composition seam: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-context/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs,tests/parity.rs}`, workspace manifest and existing `fleet` binary adapter. Do not create per-domain wrappers/crates. The facade owns dependency construction, preflight and typed operation dispatch only; policy and operation logic remain in domain owners.

Proposed API:
```rust
pub struct FleetContextBuilder { /* ARCH-01 resolver/context, ARCH-12 input/output plans,
    ARCH-06 authorization/ledger/output ports, domain services, clock */ }
pub struct FleetContext { /* immutable composed ports */ }
impl FleetContext {
    pub async fn execute(&self, request: OperationRequest, cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<OperationReceipt, ContextError>;
}
pub enum ContextError { MissingCapability, PolicyDenied, Unavailable, Partial,
                        Uncertain, Cancelled, Domain(DomainError) }
```
The builder receives authority ports/capabilities, not constructors for SigningAuthorization, DurableTupleClaim or OutputAuthorization. It may request authorization only after a domain has prepared exact bytes/tuple. CLI adapters parse/render only and call the same typed operation path. Root operations require explicit root-key identity/ceremony; no default signer exists.

## API/CLI example
```rust
let ctx = FleetContext::builder()
    .resolver(resolver).input_resolver(input_resolver)
    .signing_authorization(signing_port).tuple_ledger(ledger)
    .output_authorization(output_port).event_sink(events)
    .domain_services(fake_domains).build()?;
let receipt = ctx.execute(OperationRequest::SyntheticPipeline(plan), cancel).await?;
```
An existing Fleet domain command parses the equivalent versioned request and calls the same `execute`; this issue adds no standalone CLI. The library route never spawns Fleet. `fleet secrets get` keeps its separate legacy raw-value stdout behavior; typed structured receipts remain redacted.

## Measurable acceptance
1. One typed request through CLI adapter and embedded facade yields equivalent public result/error and redacted receipt under the same fake services.
2. An in-memory synthetic pipeline streams one fixture to two fake sinks (NATS→DB/Redis-shaped) with no process spawn, temp file or network.
3. Missing domain port returns typed MissingCapability before side effect; cancellation/partial/uncertain outcomes are preserved per operation and do not claim cross-sink atomicity.
4. Facade cannot construct or clone signer/output authority; root signing requires explicit key identity and the ARCH-06 final-tuple claim; private artifact output requires an exact output grant.
5. `fleet-connect` does not link the facade or its dependencies; minimal consumer dependency closure stays controlled by ARCH-10.

## Negative tests and oracle
MBT compares facade and CLI adapter states against a reference operation-result model. Negative cases: missing port, output mismatch, hidden subprocess, secret sentinel in structured receipt/log, duplicate effect after cancellation, root request without explicit key/ceremony/claim, private sink without destination grant, expired/wrong grant, and a facade operation bypassing domain policy. Oracle: canonical redacted request/receipt golden and fake invocation counters prove denied calls cause zero signer/sink actions.

## Security and safe environment
Synthetic values and fake services only. No live provider, production sign, secret write, NATS/DB/Redis service, deployment, schedule, DNS/trust change or root export. Builder carries explicitly injected authority ports but never mints authority.

## Dependencies, priority, lifecycle, size, stage
Parent #9157; hard dependencies ARCH-01, ARCH-06, ARCH-07 and ARCH-12. Estimated size/complexity L; V2 foundation; Backlog; intrinsic urgency 700 (High), separate from importance/stage/queue projection.

## Failure, rollback, recovery
Keep facade behind an optional feature and preserve existing direct domain APIs. On parity/authority regression disable the facade; no production state is changed. An uncertain operation is reconciled by its owning domain before retry.

## Open decisions
Validate that the facade crate has useful reuse and one-way dependency closure before extraction. Reversal trigger: if it starts owning domain policy or becomes a god object, move orchestration back to domain modules.
stage: V2 foundation; shared composition facade with domain-owned operations

1. `fleet secrets get <name>` fixture: exact stdout is the requested sentinel plus current line terminator; stderr contains no sentinel; success exit 0. Do not assert that get never prints its result value.
2. `fleet secrets list` fixture: exact broker name-only output, deterministic order, no value, and no BWS inventory fallback. Broker error exits 3 and does not silently enumerate BWS.
3. Secret usage/arity/unknown leaf arguments return 2; unresolved get returns 3; top-level unavailable compiled/profile capability stub returns 69; successful help returns 0.
4. Full/serve/connect snapshots record canonical domains, aliases, subcommands, compiled/profile/effective availability and exit status. Connect is proxy-only; its secret/queue/other unavailable behavior remains stub code 69. Existing registry invariant `connect ⊂ serve ⊂ full` continues to hold.

Use deterministic fake broker responses and a stub BWS runner. Preserve expected sentinel on successful get stdout.

Synthetic names/values only. Never invoke a live secrets broker, BWS or other vault; use a stubbed command runner/socket fixture. No CA keys, provider credentials, deployments, DNS/trust changes, or writes.

Parent #9156; no dependencies. Estimated complexity: Small/Medium (S/M); V2 foundation as V1 characterization only; High, intrinsic urgency 600; lifecycle Ready. Do Now/direct dispatch is not inferred. Urgency remains separate from importance/stage and Project/queue priority.

A changed golden is a compatibility change requiring a versioned baseline update plus an owning implementation/design issue and reviewer explanation. If a test harness requires changing production semantics, stop and retain the V1 implementation; adjust only the test seam. Removing characterization tests is not a rollback for product behavior.

## Open decisions
Decide whether stdout fixtures are captured through a private writer seam or a hermetic subprocess with fake socket/runner. Both must use the exact current V1 CLI entry path and preserve production defaults.

## Goal / user outcome
Produce reproducible evidence whether a pinned OpenBao release is a viable future machine-secrets service, without making it a Fleet or production dependency. A three-node local container cluster is a functional Raft experiment only: because all nodes share host/power/kernel/storage failure, it MUST NOT be described as highly available.

## Current evidence / prerequisites
The repo has no OpenBao adapter or production service in the intake census (`note.md` §§32–50). Official OpenBao 2.7.x docs describe Raft replication/HA, leader behavior, Shamir per-node unseal, auto-seal lifecycle dependency, audit fail-closed behavior and KV v2 features. The dated addendum §7 requests three local synthetic nodes. No cluster, provider token, real data or live credentials have been used.

## Scope and boundaries
Create a disposable, pinned image-digest lab and scripts/config in an isolated, nonproduction location. Use synthetic fixture values only. Do not write production config, repo secrets, real account data, root keys or provider credentials. Do not add Fleet code/adapters, deploy to OCI/Kubernetes, change DNS/trust, or claim uptime. Record image/version, resource budget, host topology and exact commands.

## Experiment and acceptance
1. Start three Raft nodes with separate data volumes; verify membership, leader and quorum using OpenBao status/API. 2. Exercise successful synthetic KV read/write and policy-denied cross-path read/write. 3. Inject one process loss, restart, network partition, disk-full condition, full-host stop/start and audit-sink outage/hang. 4. Take a snapshot, restore to a clean isolated data directory/cluster, and compare a known synthetic manifest. 5. Record p50/p95/p99 for a bounded fixed workload, CPU/RAM/disk, recovery wall time, lost/duplicated operations and every manual intervention. Acceptance requires reproducible commands, pinned versions, all outcomes and a topology diagram; a whole-host outage MUST demonstrate that the same-host lab is unavailable. No production claim.

Wrong token and insufficient policy must be denied; partition without quorum must fail writes rather than report success; corrupted snapshot must be rejected; absent audit sinks must show blocked or explicitly documented behavior; restored state must match fixture hashes/version metadata. Stop and remove only the disposable lab resources created by this issue. Preserve sanitized logs/config/metrics and snapshot checksums; destroy all synthetic secret values after evidence capture. No blocking prerequisite. This is research, not deployment approval. Any V3 host, OCI, Kubernetes or production work requires a separate issue and human authorization. Unknowns: actual future host, desired RPO/RTO, budget, operator coverage and release target.

Run at least 10,000 generated dependency/fault sequences against an explicit reference model. For each, output reachable authorized synthetic artifact states, shared dependencies, and whether the approved class would be available; a missing edge/key/auth dependency must change outcome from recoverable to unavailable. Invariants: two nominal copies sharing auth/key/host are not called independent; no root/recovery class enters the model; stale copies never become authoritative or write back; unauthorized class remains denied; no undocumented dependency is marked satisfied. Oracle: graph reachability plus independent policy/reference state machine, with minimized counterexamples. Remove each decryption recipient, provider-auth identity, host, seal key, bucket/account, and metadata index independently and in paired combinations; assert availability status matches reference graph. ## Current evidence and boundary
Fleet secrets currently handles named strings. `pkgs/id/src/lib.rs` has a separate sign-only-what-receipt-accepts contract (lines 54–103); do not copy/weaken it. Synthetic keys only; no root key export, production signing or provider writes.

`fleet generate key --kind <registered-id>`, `fleet key derive-public|fingerprint|inspect`, `fleet sign file|text --key <explicit-signer-ref>`, `fleet verify file|text --signature <ref> --public-key <ref>`. Root signing uses A-2 authorization bound to root fingerprint/handle, subject key identity, algorithm, profile/purpose, exact validity, artifact-plan digest and approved outputs; expiring/single-use by default.

Each enabled algorithm signs and independently verifies synthetic fixed fixture; wrong key, modified message, unsupported digest/encoding and public-only signing fail; fingerprint encoding is explicit; key format round-trips. Feature inspection proves unused algorithms absent from connect. Oracle: OpenSSL 3.5+, independent Rust verifier where supported and official vectors. Negative tests reject ambient signer lookup, signer substitution, changed plan, wrong purpose, expired/replayed root grant, silent fallback or ML-DSA claimed without verifier support.

## Dependencies, safety, priority and recovery

Fleet currently has no SSH remote operation. Use a disposable OpenSSH lab only. No production host, broad unattended policy, Fleet proxy change, secret-store reconciliation or timer work. MBT covers each transition/restart. Preserve old access until new key has a fresh successful login; injected network loss, permissions drift, failed auth, timeout or partial write halts before removing old key. A-1: remote guard is per operation; when human/other writer can alter target and no atomic precondition/serialization is proven, step is `needs-review`, or a separately approved weaker policy records the lost-update window in plan/receipt. Oracle: disposable OpenSSH server/client, host-key fingerprint, remote authorized_keys hashes/modes and independent state model. ## Outcome
Add typed `hash`, `verify-hash`, `fingerprint`, and `derive-key` primitives using reviewed standards, not a Fleet-private scheme. General content/integrity digest, public-key fingerprint and password KDF have separate types and purpose encodings. `id` BLAKE3 content identity is not a fingerprint or KDF. Low-entropy secret hashes leak equality; roots stay out of equality indices.

## Current evidence and scope
Fleet V1 has no generator crypto API. GEN-01/ARCH-06 own shared seams; GEN-10 owns capability descriptors. This issue owns concrete adapters only; no provider, root signer, password-verifier service or secret inventory.

## API/errors
Proposed `fleet hash <public-input-ref> --algorithm <id> --encoding <id>`, `fleet key fingerprint <public-key-ref> --digest <id>`, and `fleet key derive --kdf <registered-id> --profile <approved-versioned-profile> --input-stdin --length N` only with protected input and secret sink. Per-purpose allowlist: SHA-256 is required for fingerprint and DER-integrity profiles unless a protocol explicitly specifies another; SHA-2/BLAKE3 are allowed only for typed public content/integrity profiles, and BLAKE3 content identity cannot substitute for a fingerprint. MD5/SHA-1 are refused for security-sensitive purposes. Argon2id is the leading password-KDF candidate; PBKDF2/scrypt only explicit interop profiles after review. The derive-key CLI remains disabled until a versioned profile records numeric min/max memory, time/passes, parallelism, salt length and output length plus target resource budget. No secret in args/env/logs. Errors distinguish unsupported digest/KDF, invalid params, unavailable input, unsafe downgrade and output length. Server password verifier is separate scope.

## Acceptance/oracle/negative
Canonical output records algorithm/params/version/purpose/domain-separation/encoding; fingerprint identifies digest; KDF parameters are validated against a reviewed versioned profile before allocation; outputs match independent official vectors. Until numeric min/max resource and output bounds are reviewed and recorded, KDF capability reports unsupported (fail closed). KDF output is non-displayable/non-serializable, redacted and zeroized best-effort. PBT checks parse/params. Oracle: NIST FIPS 180-4 SHA-2 vectors, RFC 9106 Argon2 vectors, NIST SP 800-132 guidance, plus an independent implementation. Negative: type/purpose substitution, unsafe downgrade/reparameterization, invalid salt, malformed encoding, unbounded memory/time, low-entropy hash as equality token, private KDF result to public sink all fail.

## Dependencies/priority/lifecycle/rollback
Depends GEN-01/10 and ARCH-06. Research Rust library/MSRV/side-channel/FIPS policy and Argon2id resource profile before enabling. Open decision: key derivation vs password verifier. Standard urgency 1000, `priority/normal` projection 40, Standard importance: valuable but not V1 blocker; L, V2, Backlog. Synthetic vectors only; failures emit no output and adapter may be disabled without reinterpreting IDs.

## Priority, urgency and importance
Priority label/projection: `priority/normal` / queue 40 (the publisher derives this from the intrinsic urgency band). Intrinsic urgency: 1000 (Standard; lower is sooner), distinct from importance, blockers, lifecycle, stage and dispatch. Importance rationale: Typed hash/KDF boundaries prevent unsafe algorithm reuse and equality leakage; important crypto hygiene, gated by standards review.

V1 `secrets_broker::do_refresh` lists every BWS record visible to its token, fetches values and installs successes into the ordinary cache (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs:190-260`). Before first BWS escrow copy, trusted policy must bind exact project/native IDs and prove legacy broker/runtime principals cannot list/get/cache that scope (prefer a distinct least-privilege grant). ## Why / user outcome
Establish a repeatable synthetic benchmark before selecting cache/provider changes or claiming BWS latency is intrinsic. Produce a reproducible baseline covering Fleet's current resolver/broker and comparable provider paths, with no production secret access.

## Current evidence and affected code
Baseline commit `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e` (2026-11-12): `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs` implements broker transport then BWS CLI list/get fallback; `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs` refreshes via BWS CLI, list plus per-secret get at bounded concurrency; `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs` has only `get` and `list`. No benchmark command or Fleet provider SDK dependency is present. No performance timings have been measured. V1 describes this current-state census only; this proposal is V2-foundation.

## Deliverable and technical boundaries
Add an opt-in benchmark harness and report. Start with deterministic fake/in-process sources. Provider comparisons may include broker, direct BWS CLI, official BWS Rust SDK only after SDK parity/MSRV verification, `op` CLI, fnox CLI and published `fnox-client`, local SOPS/age decrypt, and separately authorized `bw` CLI. Keep BWS, OP and BW identities/scopes distinct. Live access, if separately authorized, is restricted to disposable isolated fixture vaults/projects. No personal/production vault reads or writes, no changes to current resolver behavior, no secret-bearing stderr/value output.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. Matrix records cold/warm process and auth; sequential and batch 1/10/100/1000 records (also 500 as intermediate); concurrency curves; batch where provider supports it; first/full paginated list/full census; cache hit/miss; synthetic create/update/readback only in disposable store; auth overhead; throttles/failures/recovery.
2. Report sample count, p50/p95/p99, quantile confidence intervals, throughput, error/timeout/throttle rate, bytes, CPU, peak/RSS memory, process count/startup, token/session churn, provider/cache age, exact versions, host/OS and RTT. Separate network, auth/startup, provider, serialization and cache latency where observable. Cover laptop and actual agent host if available; include low-concurrency 24-hour soak before systemic slowness claims. Define p99 as nearest-rank `x_(ceil(0.99 n))` over successful completed-operation latencies; `x_(i)` is the one-based i-th sorted value, retaining ties (never jitter). For IID/stationary trials, compute a two-sided equal-tail, at-least-95%-coverage nonparametric order-statistic interval: let `B~Binomial(n,0.99)`; choose the largest lower rank `k` with `P(B<k)<=0.025` and smallest upper rank `l` with `P(B>=l)<=0.025`; report `[x_(k),x_(l)]`, n, k/l, endpoints and quantile convention. Equal endpoints from ties are reported as observed. A 100-sample cell is exploratory, not reliable p99; the ≥10,000-operation floor alone does not establish interval precision. If dependence, nonstationarity or censoring invalidates IID, label p99 exploratory/unavailable or preregister a block-bootstrap method and block-length rule before seeing outcomes; never choose post hoc. Report interval width; wide/unavailable intervals cannot support superiority. Retain all attempts and report failures, timeouts and throttles separately; timed-out/censored attempts are not silently dropped.
3. Provide repeatable command and raw anonymized timings. Do not invent target values before baseline. Oracle: deterministic scripted-provider event trace validates labels/failures; independently recompute nearest-rank quantile and exact-binomial CI from sorted retained samples, including rank indices and tied endpoints. Randomized/interleaved design supports IID assumption; otherwise p99 is exploratory unless block bootstrap and block-length rule are preregistered. No benchmark was run in this design phase.
4. Synthetic canary value is absent from stdout/stderr, JSON, logs, telemetry, panic/crash output and artifacts.

## Negative tests
403/permission denial, 429/Retry-After, timeout, malformed/truncated pagination, provider absence, unsupported SDK, empty result and read-after-write mismatch remain distinct and never imply deletion. No live credentials configured by default. Harness refuses production-designated scopes.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
No implementation dependency; optional real provider runs require capability verification plus explicit isolated-vault authorization. High priority, urgency 450, medium size, V2-foundation, Ready as synthetic work.

## Rollback / recovery
Opt-in command and adapters only; disable/remove benchmark paths without changing `get/list`. No provider mutation outside disposable approved fixture and no persisted secret values.

After baseline, implementation owner proposes p95/p99 and regression budgets with workload rationale; reviewers can refine, without waiting on user-supplied thresholds or blocking the benchmark deliverable. Until then, oracle is sound reproducible measurement, not threshold attainment.

## Why / user outcome
Define one canonical, policy-owned per-secret freshness contract so cache age, provider outage, rotation and revocation cannot be confused. This proposal is the owner of freshness semantics for #9160. Related architecture, broker and reconciliation packets consume this contract; they must not invent competing max-age defaults or duplicate its policy model.

## Current evidence and affected code
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs` is an uncached redacted broker/BWS resolver. Broker code `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs` has per-secret installation, fetched timestamps, age/source, singleflight and partial-refresh behavior from merged PR #8491 (`c676d1c41c07`), with reported 59/59 tests. #6767 is still OPEN for deployment verification/live canary. That deployment/canary is not authorized in this run. V1 is current-state census, not a new implementation stage. Do not reimplement PR #8491 or claim deployed proof.

## Deliverable and technical boundaries
Specify and implement only the missing policy semantics over existing source age/provenance: cache/result states, typed max-age decision, `refresh-required`/`stale` outcomes, unavailable/inaccessible/not-found distinction, revocation precedence, and class-specific stale/offline eligibility. Preserve exact provider/account/project/vault/profile scope. Ordinary resolver/hot cache/snapshot must categorically exclude root private-key bytes, including a nominal `live-only` cache; a separately authorized bounded in-memory signer operation and encrypted root escrow are separate custody interfaces. Do not add a persistent cache, new provider, reconciliation writer, or silent legacy CLI change.

## API and behavior
Result carries source/native reference, observed revision if available, fetched-at/age, authority/cache state, class and freshness decision without revealing values. Policy chooses live-only, bounded-stale or snapshot-eligible per class; provider 403, timeout, incomplete list and unknown revocation never become absence/deletion. Successful Fleet-mediated writes must invalidate exact ordinary secret identity before reporting success; where no write path currently exists, specify contract for later consumer rather than inventing one here. Stale/snapshot data never authorizes writes or updates a provider.

## Measurable acceptance and oracle
1. A model-based test generator exercises fresh/expired age, live-only and bounded-stale classes, revocation, scoped aliases, outage/403, incomplete listing, refresh failure/success and recovery using fake clock/provider.
2. Invariants: failed refresh never advances fetched-at; age over declared maximum is denied; revocation deny wins over warm entry; 403/outage/partial inventory never means deleted; same-name secrets in distinct scopes do not alias; allowed stale responses are marked and bounded; ordinary secret write invalidation is exact and synchronous where a write API exists.
3. Existing #8491 behavior/tests are reused; add tests only for policy decisions not already covered. Existing #6767 deployment/canary remains separate; do not run canary.
4. Oracle is a versioned reference state model compared after every generated operation with fake-clock/provider traces; redaction scanner proves values absent from Debug/errors/logs/status.
5. Implementation owner derives proposed per-class initial age defaults from PERF-01 measurements plus risk rationale and records them in the reviewable policy/report. This proposal can be reviewed/refined without blocking or awaiting a user-picked numeric threshold; tests use explicit policy fixtures, not magic production timing.

## Negative tests
Over-age but otherwise valid value, revoked value, unknown age, backward clock, 403-as-absence, truncated inventory, stale divergent replica, failed refresh, same-name cross-scope collision, and cache result used as write authority all fail closed as policy requires. Root private-key bytes cannot enter or be returned by ordinary resolver/cache/snapshot tests. Live canary is expressly not an acceptance criterion.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Reuses #6767 and merged PR #8491 as implementation baseline. High priority, urgency 450, medium size, V2-foundation, Ready for synthetic/model work. Consumers are `designs/secrets.md` and `designs/reconciliation.md`; active implementation consumers are ARCH-01, SEC-03 and REC-07. They consume PERF-02’s canonical semantics and must not duplicate its policy or define competing age defaults.

## Rollback / recovery
Version policy/result behavior; high-risk classes fail closed if policy absent or malformed. Rollback cannot claim freshness or restore high-risk stale serving. Recover only by authoritative reread and exact invalidation. No live rotation, deployment, provider write, or canary.



## Priority, lifecycle and sizing
Intrinsic urgency 450 (High); queue projection 20 only if the existing queue field is populated (High→20, Standard→40, Low/Someday/Cold→70). This intrinsic score is not the queue score and is separate from importance, dependencies, lifecycle and dispatch. Size M; lifecycle Ready; stage V2-foundation; lane OpenCode implementation/test.

ML-DSA root never signs a classical root by default. Cross-certs are path candidates, never trust anchors. Each cross-signature uses ARCH-06 authorization only after final subject SPKI, serial, dates and exact TBS are frozen.

## Current evidence
V1 has no PKI. The exact root graph is specified in §3.2; §24.2 reuses that root subset in the larger graph.

## Proposed files/API

## Acceptance/oracle
This issue's own manifest equals the exact nine-root-edge table in spec §3.2; every edge has correct subject SPKI, signer issuer/AKI, distinct serial/fingerprint, signature algorithm and exact `notAfter=2050-07-07T12:00:00Z` for every root variant. An earlier cap returns `ReferenceValidityMismatch` or requires an explicit non-reference profile and new authorization; it does not pass as reference. All 13 root variants are date-checked. Reject grants created before final tuple/TBS. Verify with OpenSSL and independent verifier for supported algorithms. Oracle is exact root-edge tuple equality plus cryptographic verification.

## Negative tests
Forbidden ML-DSA-to-classical edge, wrong signer/AKI/SPKI/date, expired/substituted edge, duplicate serial, cross-cert accepted as trust anchor, unauthorized/replayed tuple, or path that claims unsupported algorithm must fail.

## Rollback/safety
Revert/deactivate only synthetic graph version and retain evidence. Strict argument preflight before side effects; no production root signing or trust publication.

Implement PKI-specific algorithm/object capability reporting and adapters through ARCH-06's shared signer/authorization interface. Race two consumers for one tuple: at most one atomic durable consume and signer invocation. Inject crashes before consume, after consume/before call, after call/before receipt, and after receipt; lost/uncertain result remains burned until authoritative signer audit reconciliation. Reject silent ML-DSA/Dilithium substitution, algorithm/backend/signature mismatch, wrong explicit source, altered tuple/TBS, pre-final grant, tuple addition after approval, expired/replayed/consumed tuple, concurrent second consumer, unsupported object, provider-version mismatch or fallback signer.

Disable optional adapter/feature and preserve receipt/test corpus. No production key material, provider writes, or ordinary-cache access.

## Outcome
Implement append-only PKI operation states, request hashes, actor/approval, signer receipt, artifact hash, idempotency and resumable batch state on #9157's shared journal/receipt contract. Do not duplicate the general Fleet journal/outbox.

## Current evidence
V1 PKI is absent. Architecture ADR-S02 classifies per-adapter/per-operation writes; BWS/op/bw are unguarded until primary evidence plus isolated test proves otherwise. A Fleet lease/readback is not serialization.

## Proposed files/interfaces
`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-pki/src/operation.rs` records PKI state and references shared #9157 journal types; per-operation guard status and plan/receipt fields support CERT-11.

## Acceptance/oracle
Inject failure before signer, after signer, CRL build, staging, upload, alias, and activation. Default unguarded conflict test does not apply and reports `needs_review`; preflight → external edit → apply leaves external value recoverable and reports conflict. A separately approved named weaker-policy test must show the lost-update window in plan+receipt and does not claim preservation. Ensure no serial reuse, duplicate signer invocation, false active status, or blind retry. Oracle is generated state schedule plus receipt and store readback.

## Negative tests
Reject last-success advancement without readback, lease-as-serialization, blind replay after uncertain timeout, partial CRL mirror, mutable-CDP rollback to lower number, overwrite after concurrent edit, and omitted weaker-policy disclosure. Additive immutable creates/history remain allowed.

## Rollback
Preserve signed/published evidence; resume only with exact request hash/authorization receipt; never delete immutable artifacts; strict whole argv before all side effects.

## Outcome
Provide reliable laptop daily execution only after safe initial migration and approved plan, with full scans periodically and incremental cursors as hints. Current repository has no secrets reconciliation schedule in V1. Root `AGENTS.md` requires the unified fleet schedule registry be updated in the same pass as any schedule change.

## Deliverable and boundary
Reusable CLI/library run contract, exact scope lock, persistent restart-after-sleep behavior, bounded retry, last-complete watermark and full-scan cadence. Timer invokes library; choose existing control plane/systemd only after repo conventions. No live schedule enablement in design pass.

## Proposed owned files and interfaces
Proposed owned files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/admin/schedule.rs`, target timer/unit only after owner selects surface, and schedule-registry update in the same implementation pass.

## Acceptance and oracle
Synthetic restart/resume retains last complete baseline; invalid cursor triggers full inventory; incomplete scope or unresolved item leaves global watermark unchanged; per-item verified baseline components persist independently; overlapping run prevented; stale lease does not take over unknown operation; tests never access real secrets. Oracle: scheduler/fake executor state assertions.

## Negative tests
Incomplete run cannot advance watermark; cursor-only absence cannot delete; no production timer before reviewed first-run migration, restore test and explicit approval.

## Dependencies / priority / lifecycle
Depends REC-01/07 and coordinate #9165. Medium (M), late V3, Standard / intrinsic urgency 1000; Backlog.

## Rollback / recovery / open decision
Disable timer, retain checkpoints/journal, run plan-only full scan when authorized. Daily time and schedule owner remain implementation/ops decision; update registry if actual schedule is created or changed.

Lane/capability: code (proposed; confirm against current registry). Urgency is the intrinsic charter score, not the queue priority field or a dispatch instruction.
